summary: A supplied vector reconstruction of the British Columbia Railway dogwood mark (five-petal version), from a railcar photograph, with its typeface identified from The Cariboo (issues 27 and 31). See package-README.md and review/preview.webp. The package's standalone emblem and wordmark are components and are not collected separately.

assets.sourceLocator: Lettering: The Cariboo, issue 31 (January 1998), flatcar article, “Painting” — the post-1972 roadname in Microgramma Bold Extended
assets.label: British Columbia Railway — Dogwood disc and wordmark (reconstruction)
assets.notes: A white dogwood with green leaves on a gold disc, beside BRITISH COLUMBIA RAILWAY on three lines in a wide, squared grotesque — white, as the railway painted it on its green equipment. The mark of the British Columbia Railway name, from 1972; it is on the cover of J. F. Garden’s book British Columbia Railway and on the company’s shoulder patch.
assets.fidelityNote: A supplied vector reconstruction, not original artwork: the dogwood is two circles, five individually drawn petals, five leaves and fifteen stamen strokes, and the fourteen capitals are custom outlines in the manner of Microgramma Bold Extended, the typeface the BC Railway Historical & Technical Society’s The Cariboo names for the post-1972 roadname. Rebuilt after a photograph of a railcar, with an enlarged flower as a check; line widths follow the photograph (636 : 898 : 759). Colours (#F8BF00, #005631) are clean approximations, not verified specifications.
